title: Japan national CPI (February 2027), 08:30 JST
source: EST: stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026'), fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes) and parsed cell-by-cell out of its single HTML table by this session. Columns are 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks'; the row parses exactly as ['February', 'March 19', 'March', 'March 26', '2026 fiscal yearly average of Ku-area of Tokyo'] — i.e. the February-2027 national CPI releases 2027-03-19, with the Tokyo March flash following 2027-03-26. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the sibling japan-cpi-2027-01-22 entry: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the schedule page's own last-update stamp is 2026-01-23 — ~19 months stale at the fetch date, and this is the LAST row the published table carries. The 08:30 JST release time is the Statistics Bureau's standing convention and is NOT read off this page — treat it as the weaker half of this entry
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-decision-2027-03-18 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and the reason it is tracked: this print lands ONE DAY AFTER the Bank of Japan's March 2027 MPM decision (boj-decision-2027-03-18, estimate), which makes that meeting the WORST-INFORMED 2027 venue on Japanese prices — the board decides on January data (released 2027-02-19, same table) while the February print sits one day out of reach. That is the exact inverse of boj-decision-2027-01-22, which meets ON its CPI release date and is the best-informed. Impact is LOW, not medium, for the same reason its January sibling is: no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI, symbols is empty, and this entry's value is corridor structure rather than a price channel. The corridor it completes is dense, and that is the point — FOMC + first SEP of 2027 on 2027-03-17, BoJ on 2027-03-18, then this print at 08:30 JST on 2027-03-19 alongside US quarterly triple witching (opex-2027-03-19, estimate) the same session. Anything read out of that three-day stretch has to be split four ways before any of it is credited to the BoJ. One caution recorded so the next session does not re-derive it: the published schedule ENDS at this row, so both the observation that would confirm this date and the one that would kill it sit on a page the Statistics Bureau has not refreshed since 2026-01-23.
